extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys/practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, disciplinary counsel, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO Final Order resolving disciplinary charges by way of a Proposed Settlement Agreement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, setting forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions for a registered patent practitioner. Includes jurisdictional bases, the factual predicate for misconduct, the specific sanctions imposed, and the requirements and procedures for reinstatement and publication of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.26
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposed Settlement Agreement sets forth certain stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and sanctions to which the OED Director and Respondent have agreed in order to resolve voluntarily a disciplinary complaint against Respondent. The Proposed Settlement Agreement, which satisfies the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26, resolves all disciplinary action by the United States Patent and Trademark Office arising from the stipulated facts set forth below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement under § 11.26 must include stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed sanctions and, if approved, results in a Final Order that disposes of the disciplinary action arising from those stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdictional basis
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary matters before the USPTO are governed by the cited statutes and regulations; any Final Order should cite the statutory/regulatory bases for jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner subject to USPTO disciplinary rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At all times relevant hereto, Respondent ... has been an attorney registered to practice before the Office and is subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners are subject to 37 C.F.R. Part 10 ethical rules; factual findings about registration and applicability should be stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline based on state suspension (37 C.F.R. § 10.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent acknowledges that his conduct violated 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(a) and 10.23(b)(6), via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5), by being suspended for a period of three years from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of the State of Florida and by being suspended for a period of one year and one day from the practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of the State of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A suspension or similar disciplinary action by a state authority for ethical grounds is a predicate for USPTO discipline under § 10.23; Final Orders will identify the state proceedings and specific rule violations relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal conviction and related misconduct as disciplinary predicate
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent pled guilty ... to one count of knowingly and willfully making a materially false, fictitious, and fraudulent statement in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 1001. Respondent was convicted and sentenced ... and fined $200,000. Mr. Snyder's respective suspensions ... were predicated upon his pleading guilty to making false statements on a financial disclosure form and his subsequent criminal conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions (e.g., for making false statements) and related misconduct that reflect adversely on a lawyer's honesty and fitness can form the basis for suspension by state bars and subsequent USPTO disciplinary action; the Final Order should describe the conviction and its relationship to the state disciplinary findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to disclose outside employment/financial disclosure violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent ... continued to operate his litigation consulting business and did not submit required forms requesting approval or report participation in MLFS or income received. From 2003 through 2005, Respondent submitted annual financial disclosures ... failing to report income received from MLFS totaling approximately $589,450.00.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to follow required reporting/approval processes and making materially false statements on financial disclosure forms are factual bases that may support professional discipline; the Order documents the specific omissions and amounts involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanction — suspension from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for a period of thirty-six (36) months from the practice of patent, trademark, and non-patent law before the USPTO commencing on the date the Final Order is signed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies the duration and scope of suspension (patent, trademark, and non-patent practice). Sanctions should be clearly stated with commencement date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during suspension
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disbarred/suspended practitioners must comply with § 11.58 (duties of disciplined practitioners), and the Final Order can require explicit compliance as a condition of the sanction and for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to facilitate compliance with § 11.58(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Final Order is signed and expiring thirty (30) days after the date the Final Order is signed for the sole purpose of facilitating Respondent's compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A temporary, narrowly limited recognition period may be granted solely to allow a disciplined practitioner to wind down or comply with duties (e.g., client notifications) required by § 11.58(b). The Order must state the limited purpose and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO customer numbers and PKI certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO promptly dissociate Respondent's name from all USPTO customer numbers and public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificates; Respondent not use any USPTO customer number or PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated ...; Respondent not obtain a USPTO customer number or a PKI certificate unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders will typically direct the USPTO to dissociate practitioner access credentials and bar the disciplined practitioner from using or obtaining customer numbers/PKI until formal reinstatement to protect the integrity of filings and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent remain suspended ... until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement based upon Respondent showing proof to the satisfaction of the OED Director, as required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60(c), that: (1) Respondent has the good moral character and reputation, competency, and learning in law required under 37 C.F.R. § 11.7 for admission, (2) the resumption of Respondent's practice before the Office will not be detrimental to the administration of justice or subversive to the public interest; and (3) Respondent has complied with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 for the full period of suspension; Respondent comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 when seeking reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement petitions must satisfy § 11.60(c) and demonstrate the practitioner's moral character, competence (per § 11.7), lack of detriment to administration of justice, and full compliance with § 11.58 during suspension. The Order points to the standards and procedures for seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room ...; the OED Director publish the following Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final disciplinary orders are published in the OED Reading Room and Official Gazette, and notice is sent to relevant state disciplinary authorities and courts per § 11.59; Orders should include a published notice summarizing the suspension and its grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the disciplinary record in future matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of this disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, be considered (1) when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct brought to the attention of the Office, and/or (2) in any future disciplinary proceeding (a) as an aggravating factor to be taken into consideration in determining any discipline to be imposed and/or (b) to rebut any statement or representation by or on Respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Orders state that the record may be used against the practitioner in future complaints or proceedings and may serve as an aggravating factor or to rebut future representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs between parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and Respondent bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may specify that each party bears its own costs; Orders should state cost allocation.
